name: MonarchCalloutBlock
title: CalloutBlock
summary: A highlighted block inside a document: a tone, an optional icon and any content. The display form of the document callout block.
whenToUse: To set a tip, a warning or a note apart from the text around it in an article, a help page or a rendered document.
whenNotToUse: For a message about the state of a screen, with a title and an action, use MonarchBanner. For a transient confirmation use a Snackbar.
api: @Composable fun MonarchCalloutBlock(text: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Neutral, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, toneLabel: String? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchCalloutBlock(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, tone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Neutral, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, toneLabel: String? = null, content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)

options.name: text
options.description: One paragraph of text. First overload.

options.name: tone
options.description: Selects the tint, the border, the icon color and the spoken name.

options.name: icon
options.description: An icon at the start in the tone color, hidden from TalkBack. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: toneLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name of the tone (the shared tone names in strings_internal.xml).

options.name: content
options.description: The content, in a column with an 8dp gap. Second overload.

states.name: default
states.description: Not interactive; one look per tone. Interactive content inside keeps its own behavior.

appearance: A tinted fill with a 1dp border and 12dp corners: the subtle background and subtle border for neutral, the tone's subtle fill and border otherwise. The icon takes the tone's strong color and the text the default text color, in every theme.
platformNotes: Only the display form is offered, as on iOS. The web component is also a node of the rich-text editor with a tone picker above the text (the toolbar slot, CalloutBlockExtension and its messages); that editing form belongs to a block editor, which Monarch for Android does not have. The web and iOS draw a built-in icon per tone; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the icon is an optional slot and the tone is spoken by the block instead. The danger tone is spoken "Error", as on iOS.
accessibility: The block is a traversal group whose content description is the name of the tone ("Warning"), read before the content; the neutral tone has none.
toneLabel replaces the name of the tone.
The icon is hidden from TalkBack.
The content keeps its own elements, so buttons and links inside it are reachable and work.
Text wraps and grows with the font size setting.
edgeCases: Long text wraps inside the block.
Text in the content that sets its own style or color keeps it.
Without an icon the tone shows only as the tint; say it in the text when it matters to sighted readers.
